lineage.strategy: Acquire current issuer quarterly results that quantify execution, liquidity, mix and a material expectations reset.

observations.fact: Serve reported Q2 2026 revenue of $3.238M, up 404% year over year and 9% sequentially, with recurring revenue above 50% of total revenue and $240.4M of cash and marketable securities at June 30.

Serve revised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $9M-$10M because Uber Eats delivery volume was below expectations, while lowering non-GAAP operating-expense guidance to $140M-$150M; DoorDash-derived revenue grew nearly 50% sequentially.

risks.risk: Q2 cost of revenues of $12.017M materially exceeded $3.238M of revenue, producing an $8.779M gross loss; rapid top-line growth has not yet established positive gross economics.
The guidance reduction explicitly identifies lower-than-expected Uber Eats volume, demonstrating material platform-demand dependence even as DoorDash and other verticals diversify the network.

contradictions.statementB: Q2 2026 guidance was revised to $9M-$10M due to lower Uber Eats delivery volume.
contradictions.resolution: Treat the newer Q2 guidance as current expectations evidence; Alpha should not extrapolate the earlier outlook.

unknowns.unknown: Unit economics and utilization by delivery platform/robot cohort remain insufficiently disclosed to establish normalized fleet profitability.

recommendation: Use the Q2 results as current execution evidence with both growth/liquidity positives and the material guidance reset/gross-loss negatives. Alpha retains numeric underwriting authority.
